_comment: Copy this to ~/.codex/hooks.json. This file didn't originally exist on this machine.
Measured (codex-cli 0.155.1): a hand-dropped hooks.json is untrusted by
default, and an untrusted hook is silently skipped with no message — brief
never runs. `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` bypasses that
check but is only a flag used for this measurement, not a standing install
method. To actually use this file, you must approve it once through
Codex's own hook-trust procedure — the exact steps aren't confirmed by
this repo, so follow `codex`'s own docs/help.
If the hook isn't trusted, neither the mark nor brief command in this file
runs. Even without Codex-side mark, Claude Code-side mark backfills the
ledger by having the codex-cli adapter's discover() scan rollout files
directly (via:"scan", cli.py), so the Codex→Claude direction still works
without this hook. Conversely, Claude→Codex still needs this file's brief
to actually run, so if the hook isn't trusted, only that direction
delivers nothing — it's no longer 'both directions die'. deliver() (Path B
included) only runs inside this file's brief call, so if that call never
happens, Path B/outbox never turns on either. Path B/outbox only opens
when brief actually ran but install_handoff failed — typically when
~/.codex/hooks.json has no omhc hook but brief runs anyway (e.g. manual
`omhc brief --harness codex-cli`), but other exceptions like a ~/.omhc
write failure take the same path too.
Codex has no exit hook and no compaction hook. All 6 kinds fire on
'something starting', so capture is only possible as a delayed
retroactive collection at the next session start — which is why Ctrl-C
and crashes are not a problem by definition.
Measured (codex-cli 0.155.1, --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust): a top-level
{"additionalContext": …} (--wire sdk) is rejected as 'hook: SessionStart
Failed' and nothing gets injected. Only --wire claude (nested
hookSpecificOutput) actually shows up in the rollout as
content_item_kinds=["hooks.additional_context"].
